changes: Unite, Intersect, Subtract, Differ compare signed native Extent before/after rather than unsigned Rust len.
Intersection selects its traversal side by signed Extent and exits after clear when either source is empty; Subtract restores its empty-input shortcut.

A shared private cursor loop applies each mutation before advancing; Union initializes its second iterator only after finishing the first source. Intersect/Intersection/Difference preserve per-key selection before insertion.
Differ explicitly checks Contains before Remove/Add, preserving native lookup sequence for custom callback behavior.

Existing legacy members, four explicit unary self operations and four binary operand-alias adapters retain their bodies and now exercise corrected algorithms. No allocator/ownership or bucket_policy.rs edits.

synthetic_scope.native: Private myExtent injection with -fno-access-control, compile-time int32/size_t64 assertions. Reconstruction writes a real result; unchanged source counts are restored after Intersection; mutated change-probe counts are restored to actual enumerated cardinality.
synthetic_scope.rust: Only cfg(test) child modules write private count. No public setter. Selected sources restore original counts; change probes restore actual enumerated cardinality after recording output.
synthetic_scope.scope: 516 synthetic rows establish signed changed-return comparisons and smaller-source traversal selection over tiny graphs. They do not prove giant-map storage/traversal parity. Change probes avoid unsigned count overflow/underflow.

failure_scope.native: Standard::AllocateOptimal is interposed and throws integer17 before malloc. Successful calls retain malloc and pinned Standard Free pairing. No GlobalAlloc unwind, host exhaustion or null-return crash is attempted.
failure_scope.rust: Existing cfg(test) bucket observation::capture(true) throws before the raw allocation call. No allocator or observation implementation changes.
failure_scope.mid_operation_prefix: Four wide key types, Unite/Differ, free/member paths begin with101 nodes. First new key commits node102; the next insertion triggers resize failure. Exact resulting metadata/order and retention of all prior node addresses match native. Strict Miri checks lifetime/provenance/teardown.
failure_scope.callback_panics: Custom PackedInteger is a Rust extension. A next-block conversion panic proves each current mutation committed first; Intersect retains its original map while dropping its temporary result. A right-source conversion panic proves Union finished its left pass first. These compare source-defined order, not a native custom-key callback oracle.
failure_scope.limitation: Global node-allocation failure and arbitrary allocator policies are not injected in this slice; the pre-existing native fatal-null policy and custom-word rehash guarantees remain separate.

self_alias_scope: 144 new native unary self rows plus all1152 existing native binary destination/source alias rows are regenerated and compared byte-for-byte; the corresponding16 Rust alias tests run normally and under strict Miri. Exact264 original names are preserved.
regression_evidence: Baseline10 passed/6 failed on unmodified algorithms; final changed-return boundary and node-retention observations extend those tests. OnceLock decodes the full committed immutable numeric fixture once; no oracle assertions are filtered.

miri_exclusions.reason: Only six existing positive libc-backtrace iterator tests are excluded; all264 originals,16 alias tests,15 no-scratch allocation tests and16 new mutation tests run.

bindings.scope: Native mutation/traversal/shortcut and changed-return contracts; exact ordinary and injected bucket-failure state traces. Synthetic counts establish signed extent control flow, not giant-set execution. No global completion credit.
